Subject: Final redlines + pricing for pilot - NorthBay

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We ran the proposed pilot contract by our legal and procurement teams and attached our redlines (NorthBay_Redlines.docx). High level asks:

- Liability cap: we need a cap of $2,000,000 for the pilot term (12 months).
- Indemnity: we propose broadening indemnity carveouts for data processed on our systems; we also want Redwood to retain IP indemnity for third-party model components.
- Warranty: request a 90-day remedy period and a specific performance SLA credit tied to monthly availability.
- Pricing: procurement is pushing for a 30% first-year discount in exchange for a 24-month deployment commitment and a reference case.

We want to move quickly — procurement hopes to finalize terms next week to align with internal board approvals. Would appreciate a short internal note on what you can accept and what needs exec/legal clearance.

Attachments: NorthBay_Redlines.docx (redline), NorthBay_SOW.xlsx (separate)

- Liability cap moved to $2M (deal size: ~ $520k ARR first year; pilot value ~$210k). This exceeds our standard $1M cap for pilot engagements.
- Indemnity: they want expanded customer indemnities tied to third-party model components and data processed under their configs.
- Warranty/SLA: they want a 90-day remedy plus service credit schedule (not standard).

Marissa — they need an answer fast (board timing). If we approve a deeper discount and raise the cap, it will materially impact unit economics — can you quantify impact and confirm if Sales leadership is willing to push for the reference-case trade?

I'll set up a quick 30-min sync.

Jordan / Marissa — reviewed the attached NorthBay_Redlines.docx. High-level legal assessment:

- Liability cap: their requested $2M cap for the pilot term is outside our delegated approval for AE-level signoff. Anything above $1M requires Deal Desk + GC/Chief review. For contracts with reference obligations and multi-year commitments we can consider an exceptions committee approval path, but we need to document mitigation (insurance, aggregate cap across companies, escrow).

- Indemnity: the proposed language expands their indemnities to cover third-party models and includes reverse indemnity elements that are asymmetric. We must not accept open-ended IP indemnities for third-party models; propose we include a carveout clarifying Redwood's responsibility is limited to Redwood-originated model assets and to willful misconduct.

- Warranty / SLA: a 90-day remedy period is acceptable, but the SLA credit schedule they propose is unusually punitive for pilot scope. Recommend a capped credit (e.g., pro rata credit not exceeding one monthly invoice) and a requirement that remediation steps be attempted before credit issuance.

Recommended parallel approach for Deal Desk memo:
- Commercial: up to 25% first-year discount acceptable with 24-month commitment and signed reference. Anything >25% requires VP Sales signoff.
- Liability cap: authorize up to $1.5M on pilot if Customer agrees to specific risk mitigations (cyber insurance minimum coverage 10M, NC indemnity narrow language, no punitive credits). For $2M request, escalate to Chief + legal execs for approval.
- Indemnity: propose counter language limiting Redwood's indemnity to Redwood-provided IP and direct damages tied to breach of our obligations.

If you want, I will draft the memo and a short two-paragraph exec summary for approval (GC + Chief). I'll attach redline snippets for quick review.

Attachments: redline_summary.pdf (I'll produce this in the morning)

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Final redlines + pricing for pilot - NorthBay

All — thanks for the quick read, Laura. Commercial context from my side:

- NorthBay is a strategically important health system in our target region and will be a high-value reference for future healthcare deals. The pilot ARR/first-year revenue profile puts this in the sweet spot for a reference trade.
- Finance ran numbers: 30% discount would push the first-year unit economics to a negative margin on the pilot; 25% is achievable with delivery constraints and an onboarding fee of $25k to offset initial professional services.
- If Legal will allow up to $1.5M cap with the guardrails Laura outlined, Sales leadership will accept 25% discount + onboarding fee + signed reference commitment.

Requests:
- Jordan — please get me confirm from the procurement contact that they can accept the onboarding fee line item. If yes, I'll prepare the commercial term sheet reflecting 25% first-year discount, onboarding fee, and 24-month term.
- Laura — please draft the two-paragraph memo for GC/Chief that justifies a $1.5M cap with the proposed mitigations (insurance, narrow indemnity). If GC approves escalation to Chief, we can present the memo to Chief for final sign-off.

Timing: NorthBay's procurement wants a response by EOD Tue (6/5) to meet their board window. I'll be available for the approval call this afternoon if we need to loop in Deal Desk / VP Sales.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales
